verdict: Microsoft grew 12% to $69.6B as Azure jumped 31% and its AI business passed a $13 billion annual run rate — it kept $24.1B as profit, even as the data-center buildout pushed costs up and investment losses weighed below the line.

segments.name: Productivity and Business Processes
segments.note: Office 365, LinkedIn and Dynamics — Microsoft 365 Commercial cloud grew 16% and LinkedIn 9%.

segments.name: Intelligent Cloud
segments.note: Azure and server products — Azure and other cloud services grew 31%, the fastest-growing large piece.

segments.name: More Personal Computing
segments.note: Windows, Xbox and search ads — search and news advertising up 21%, Xbox content and services up 2%.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Spending on building products, led by AI and cloud — up 11% YoY.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling and marketing the product line — up 3% YoY.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company day to day — down 8% YoY.

follow100Note: The rows reconcile to the $34.62 kept as profit within $0.01 of rounding; other expense is a $3.29 drag per $100 of revenue.
footerNote: Segments use Microsoft's FY25 reporting structure (three segments).

takeaways.title: Azure is the growth engine
takeaways.text: Azure and other cloud services grew 31%, and Microsoft said its AI business has passed an annual revenue run rate of $13 billion — up 175% year over year.

takeaways.title: The cloud is most of Microsoft now
takeaways.text: Microsoft Cloud revenue hit $40.9B, up 21% — about 59% of all revenue. The growth story is the data centers.

takeaways.title: The PC side stood still
takeaways.text: More Personal Computing was flat at $14.7B: search ads (+21%) and Windows (+4%) offset a soft quarter for Xbox content and services (+2%).
